A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPO research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised, and added content.

before.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original TinyStories alignment experiments comparing SPO and DPO, including measured win rates throughout training.

after.justification: Section 7 and Tables 1–4 report original question-answering and story-alignment experiments, including regularizer ablations. Appendices D–E document their implementation and data generation.

M1.justification: V4 adds best-of-n and ranked-preference objectives beyond v1's pairwise method (Section 5, Eqs. 16–17). It also replaces the SoftImportance weighting formula in v1 Eq. 24 with a differently scaled, power-based formula in v4 Eq. 13. Intermittent online sampling and token-wise KL regularization already existed in v1.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates pairwise preference alignment on TinyStories-derived stories. V4 adds AlpacaFarm question answering evaluated through AlpacaEval 2, and replaces the pairwise story experiment with four-story ranking and best-of-n alignment tasks (Sections 7.1–7.2).

E2.justification: Beyond v1's DPO comparison, v4 evaluates IPO, KTO, CPO, R-DPO, and SimPO alongside DPO on AlpacaFarm (Table 1). The story comparisons add S-DPO and Best-response-SFT; Table 2 evaluates a ranking adaptation of DPO, while Table 3 does not include DPO.

E3.justification: The story experiments change from GPT3.5-Turbo labeling and evaluation to GPT4o-2024-08-06, approximately 100,000 retained pairs to 5,000 four-story groups, and batches of 128 pairs to 32 groups. The win-rate opponent changes from the pretrained model to Best-response-SFT. The new question-answering protocol uses Llama2-7B, four training epochs, GPT4-Turbo evaluation, and both conventional and length-controlled win rates.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 1 compares weighting choices and DPO regularization coefficients over training. V4 removes those trajectories and adds a controlled comparison of global KL against three dataset-restricted regularizers (Table 4). Weighting analyses extend to question answering, ranking, and best-of-n alignment, including a reported lack of benefit for ranking.

E5.justification: V1 averages story win rates over 1,000 pairs without quantifying their estimation uncertainty. V4 Appendix D.2 uses the same evaluation sample count and newly reports an estimation-error standard deviation below 0.015. This is not evidence of repeated training runs; neither version reports training-seed variability or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: V1's 72% SPO versus 68% DPO peak win rates and subsequent training trajectories are replaced by results under different settings. V4 Table 1 reports SPO at 61.63% conventional and 56.25% length-controlled win rate, versus DPO at 59.16% and 51.26%. Tables 2–3 add SPO ranking and best-of-n win rates of 68.5% and 70.5% against Best-response-SFT. These are new comparisons, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V4 adds formal n-ary preference assumptions, Theorems 3–4 for best-of-n and ranked preferences, and their proofs in Appendices B–C, including a new supporting inequality lemma. The pairwise Theorems 1–2 and the central Appendix A proof argument are largely retained.

C1.justification: The abstract drops v1's claim of comparative computational efficiency. The central abstract and introduction claims remain: reward-model-free alignment, global regularization, and adjustable softmax convergence under the BT assumption. The technical extensions do not substantially rewrite this central framing.

C2.justification: V4 Section 9 explicitly identifies unexamined dependence on dataset size and preference-label noise, and learning from implicit preferences as future work. Computational overhead from online sampling and the token-wise KL bias–variance tradeoff were already discussed in v1 Section 5 and Appendix B.

D1.justification: V4 newly documents accelerator configurations, including four H100 GPUs for AlpacaFarm and A100 GPUs for TinyStories, gradient accumulation, method-specific hyperparameter ranges, ranking-weight decay settings, and four-story labeling and filtering instructions (Appendices D–E). The existing practice of generating 32 regularization samples every eight steps is retained for TinyStories.

R1.justification: V4 substantially expands positioning through Nash/game-based alignment, token-level DPO, KTO, SimPO, and R-DPO discussions. Section 8 also explicitly positions CPO as concurrent work sharing SPO's basic contrastive loss, distinguishing SPO through global regularization, weighting, additional preference types, and theoretical guarantees.

P1.justification: V4 moves practical KL computation from the appendix into the main algorithm section, condenses the SPO–DPO comparison, reorganizes experiments into three subsections, and separates experimental settings and dataset generation into Appendices D–E. It also adds a Limitations section, renames method sections, and changes numbered citations to author-year citations.

P2.justification: V1's training-curve figure is removed. V4 adds four result and ablation tables, including side-by-side ranking and best-of-n tables, plus an algorithm display. The main-text story prompt and worked response are replaced by a different, full-page ranking-prompt display in Appendix E.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses v1's reliance on one small synthetic story task against DPO by adding 7B question answering, broader baselines, length-controlled evaluation, and direct regularizer ablations. These provide substantially more informative empirical support, alongside formalized preference extensions and expanded implementation details. Losing the training curves, limited uncertainty reporting, and the unresolved 'xx%' placeholder in Section 7.3 weaken reporting, but do not outweigh these gains.
